mainTopic: Can a slave be circumcised and brought into Judaism against his will? רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the רבנן argue, and the גמרא explains the פסוק each side uses (״כׇּל עֶבֶד אִישׁ״). שמואל uses the same פסוק to teach that a master who gives up ownership of his slave sets him free.
overview: This amud opens with the last words of רב ששת's proof from the יפת תואר. רבא then explains why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that an adult slave may be circumcised against his will: he reads ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״ as 'a slave who is an adult man.' According to עולא, the רבנן hold that no adult, slave or free, may be circumcised against his will. They use ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״ for שמואל's rule instead: a slave whose master gives up ownership goes free without a גט שחרור. רב פפא then challenges רב ששת. He says a slave, who already keeps some מצוות, may not need to accept the מצוות even according to the רבנן, and he supports this with a ברייתא about a slave bought from a non-Jew. A phrase from the conversion ברייתא seems to contradict him, but the גמרא explains that it refers only to טבילה. Next the גמרא turns to the יפת תואר. רבי אליעזר says 'doing her nails' means cutting them, and רבי עקיבא says it means letting them grow. A פסוק about מפיבשת supports רבי אליעזר. The amud ends as a new ברייתא begins on her weeping for her parents, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the proof: he would be permitted to her immediately
steps.stepSummary: The last words of רב ששת's proof from the case of the captive woman (יפת תואר). If a slave could be made Jewish without accepting the מצוות, the soldier could simply do that and marry her right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he would be permitted to her immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an argument that started before this section. It ends by saying that the soldier would then be allowed to marry the woman right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is this: make the captive a slave, then immerse her for the sake of freedom, and she would be Jewish at once. The Torah does not mention that shortcut, and the רבנן do not suggest it either. רב ששת takes that as a sign that, for the רבנן, even a slave must accept the מצוות to become Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: permitted to her (allowed to marry her)

phrases.english: And he is permitted to her immediately.
phrases.notes: This is the end of an argument from just before this section, about the captive woman taken in war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב ששת's proof, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן require a slave to accept the מצוות in order to become Jewish.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of יפת תואר: the Torah gives her a long process instead of the quick route through slavery.

steps.title: רבא explains רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's source
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק about who may eat the קרבן פסח. He reads ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״ as 'a slave who is an adult man,' and learns that such a slave may be circumcised against his will, while a free adult may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר? It is written: 'Every slave of a man bought for money.' Does 'slave of a man' mean a man's slave and not a woman's slave? No. Rather, a 'slave who is a man' you may circumcise against his will, but a 'son who is a man' (a free adult) you may not circumcise against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who holds that you may circumcise a slave against his will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word אִישׁ cannot be there to exclude a woman's slave, because that makes no sense. So רבא reads it as describing the slave himself: an adult. The lesson is that even an adult slave can be circumcised against his will. A free adult, a בֶּן אִישׁ, cannot be.

keyTerms.meaning: a slave of a man / a slave who is an adult man
a 'son who is a man': a free adult, not a slave

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר —
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar?
As it is written: "Every slave of a man that is bought for money."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:44, about who may eat the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: "A slave of a man" — and not the slave of a woman?
Rather, a "slave who is a man" —
you may circumcise against his will,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מָל בֶּן אִישׁ בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ.
phrases.english: but you may not circumcise a "son who is a man" against his will.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב ששת's proof to the source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An adult slave may be circumcised against his will, while a free adult may not.

steps.title: How do the רבנן deal with this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן respond to רבא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word sets up the next move. The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, understand the matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא has just shown a source in the פסוק for circumcising a slave against his will. So the גמרא wants to know how the other side would answer.

keyTerms.meaning: and the Sages (what do they say?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the opposing view to the source רבא just gave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן hold, and how they get around the פסוק.

steps.title: עולא: a slave is like a free adult
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that for the רבנן, just as a free adult cannot be circumcised against his will, an adult slave cannot be either.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Just as you may not circumcise a free adult against his will, so too you may not circumcise an adult slave against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the opinion of the רבנן: an adult slave is treated the same as a free adult. Neither can be circumcised against his will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר made a difference between a slave and a free person. The רבנן do not. For them, both need to agree.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מָל בֶּן אִישׁ בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as you may not circumcise a son who is a man against his will,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אִי אַתָּה מָל עֶבֶד אִישׁ בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ.
phrases.english: so too you may not circumcise a slave who is a man against his will.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מָל בֶּן אִישׁ בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן treat an adult slave like a free adult: neither may be circumcised against his will.

steps.title: But the פסוק says 'slave of a man'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן: what do they do with the words ״כׇּל עֶבֶד אִישׁ״, which רבא used as a source?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written 'every slave of a man'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the רבנן. The פסוק seems to support רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so how can they ignore it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word אִישׁ needs to teach something. If the רבנן do not learn רבא's lesson from it, the גמרא wants to know what lesson they do learn.

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "Every slave of a man"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's version of the רבנן using the פסוק from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's position as explained by עולא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word אִישׁ seems to teach that a slave may be circumcised against his will, which goes against the רבנן.

steps.title: The פסוק is needed for שמואל's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the words ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״ for a different lesson, the one שמואל teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed for what שמואל taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the רבנן. They do read the word אִישׁ as teaching something, just not what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ means these words are already being used for a different lesson. Since the רבנן need these words for שמואל's rule, they are not left over to teach רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's idea. The next step quotes שמואל.

phrases.english: That verse is needed for that which Shmuel said.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is used for a different lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word אִישׁ must teach that a slave can be circumcised against his will.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, the word אִישׁ teaches שמואל's rule about a master giving up ownership of his slave.

steps.title: שמואל: a slave his master gives up goes free
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that if a master declares his slave ownerless (הפקר), the slave goes free without a גט שחרור. He learns this from ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״: only a slave whose master still has rights over him counts as a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: One who makes his slave ownerless, the slave goes free and does not need a גט שחרור, as it says 'every slave of a man bought for money.' Does it mean a man's slave and not a woman's? No. Rather, a slave whose master has rights over him is called a slave, and one whose master has no rights over him is not called a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמואל's teaching, which shows how the רבנן use the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״ as 'a slave who belongs to a man,' meaning his master still has power over him. Once the master gives up ownership, he is no longer 'a slave of a man.' So the slave goes free even without a document.

keyTerms.meaning: one who gives up ownership (makes something הפקר, ownerless)

steps.whatToRemember: The same words ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״ teach one lesson for each side. For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, an adult slave may be circumcised against his will. For the רבנן, it is שמואל's rule that a slave his master gave up goes free without a גט שחרור.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ways of reading ״עֶבֶד אִישׁ״. רבא reads it as 'a slave who is an adult man.' שמואל reads it as 'a slave who belongs to a man,' meaning his master still owns him.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule is an important הלכה about freeing slaves: giving up ownership alone sets the slave free.

phrases.english: As Shmuel said:
One who renounces ownership of his slave — the slave goes out to freedom
and he does not need a bill of emancipation,
as it is stated: "Every slave of a man that is bought for money."
"A slave of a man" — and not the slave of a woman?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: עֶבֶד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְרַבּוֹ עָלָיו — קָרוּי עֶבֶד,
phrases.english: Rather: a slave whose master has rights over him is called a slave,
phrases.notes: Here אִישׁ means the master: the slave still 'belongs to a man.'

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵין רְשׁוּת לְרַבּוֹ עָלָיו — אֵין קָרוּי עֶבֶד.
phrases.english: and one whose master has no rights over him is not called a slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַמַּפְקִיר עַבְדּוֹ יָצָא לְחֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching mentioned in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave whose master gives up ownership of him goes free and does not need a גט שחרור.

steps.title: רב פפא: Maybe a Slave Differs From a Captive Woman
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects that the רבנן's demand for קבלת מצוות may apply only to a יפת תואר, not to a slave who already kept מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: You heard that the רבנן require accepting the מצוות for a יפת תואר, who had no connection to מצוות. But a slave already has a share in מצוות, so perhaps even the רבנן agree that he does not need to accept them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב ששת's claim about what the רבנן would say about a freed slave. He suggests that a slave is different from a יפת תואר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had assumed that the רבנן's rule about a יפת תואר also covers a freed slave. רב פפא points to a real difference: a non-Jewish slave of a Jew is already obligated in some מצוות, while a captive woman was not. So the רבנן's demand to accept the מצוות may only apply to someone starting from nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it (a sharp challenge from a later אמורא)
Say that you heard (granted, you know this much, but...)
A beautiful captive woman taken in war

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objects to it:
phrases.notes: "It" is רב ששת's earlier claim that the רבנן would make a freed slave accept the מצוות.

phrases.english: Say that you heard the Rabbis [require it]
regarding a beautiful captive woman,
who was not involved in מצוות.
But a slave, who is involved in מצוות,
perhaps indeed even the Rabbis agree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to רב ששת's claim about the רבנן and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the רבנן require a freed slave to accept the מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave already keeps some מצוות, unlike a יפת תואר. So the רבנן's demand for her cannot automatically be applied to him.

steps.title: A ברייתא Requiring Acceptance Only for a Slave Bought From a Non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא cites a ברייתא that requires acceptance of מצוות for a convert and for a slave bought from a non-Jew. He infers that a slave bought from a Jew does not need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Both a גר and someone who buys a slave from a non-Jew must have them accept the מצוות. This implies that if he bought the slave from a Jew, the slave does not need to accept them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a ברייתא to support his point. He reads an implication from its exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא specifically says "a slave bought from a non-Jew." That suggests a slave bought from a Jew is different. Such a slave already lived under מצוות in a Jewish home, so he does not need to accept them again.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Needs to accept (the yoke of מצוות)
This implies (an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גֵּר וְאֶחָד לוֹקֵחַ עֶבֶד מִן הַגּוֹי
phrases.english: Both a convert and one who buys a slave from a non-Jew
needs to accept [the מצוות].
This implies: one who buys from a Jew
does not need to accept.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֶחָד גֵּר וְאֶחָד לוֹקֵחַ עֶבֶד מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support from a ברייתא for רב פפא's objection.
steps.raayaObject: A slave who already belonged to a Jew does not need to accept the מצוות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that requires acceptance only for a slave bought from a non-Jew.

steps.title: The ברייתא Must Follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cannot follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who never requires acceptance. So it follows the רבנן, and even they exempt a slave bought from a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It cannot be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, because he says even a slave bought from a non-Jew need not accept the מצוות. So it must be the רבנן. Learn from this that, according to them, a slave bought from a non-Jew must accept, but one bought from a Jew need not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out whose opinion the ברייתא follows. This finishes רב פפא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only matters if the ברייתא follows the רבנן. Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר never requires acceptance, the ברייתא's demand must come from the רבנן. That shows the רבנן exempt a slave bought from a Jew, just as רב פפא argued.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that a freed slave never needs to accept the מצוות
Learn from it (a conclusion is drawn)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, even the רבנן require acceptance of מצוות only for a slave coming from a non-Jew. A slave who already served a Jew is exempt.

phrases.english: Whose [opinion] is this?
If Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
didn't he say: one who buys from a non-Jew also
does not need to accept!
Rather, is it not the Rabbis?
And learn from it:
that one who buys from a non-Jew
needs to accept,
but one who buys from a Jew
does not need to accept.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ברייתא from the previous step follows the רבנן, which completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן agree that a slave bought from a Jew need not accept the מצוות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Ruling out רבי שמעון בן אלעזר as the author of the ברייתא.

steps.title: A Phrase That Seems to Require a Freed Slave to Accept
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא with the phrase "both a convert and a freed slave." This phrase seems to require every freed slave to accept the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then there is a difficulty: the ברייתא says "both a גר and a freed slave"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem for רב פפא's conclusion. It points to a phrase in the earlier ברייתא about how a גר is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That phrase places a freed slave next to a גר, with no difference between kinds of slaves. It seems to mean that any freed slave must accept the מצוות, just like a convert. That would contradict רב פפא's claim that a slave bought from a Jew is exempt.

phrases.english: But then it is difficult:
"both a convert and a freed slave"!
phrases.notes: These words end the earlier ברייתא about how a גר is accepted, which talks about accepting the מצוות and then about immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא קַשְׁיָא אֶחָד גֵּר וְאֶחָד עֶבֶד מְשׁוּחְרָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion just drawn in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's conclusion that the רבנן exempt a slave bought from a Jew from accepting the מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts every freed slave together with a גר, which suggests acceptance is required for all freed slaves.

steps.title: That Phrase Is About Immersion Only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the phrase "both a convert and a freed slave" refers only to the need for טבילה. It does not refer to accepting the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that phrase was taught, it was taught about immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty. It explains that the phrase points back to a different topic in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions immersion right before this phrase, so "both a גר and a freed slave" means both need טבילה. It says nothing about accepting the מצוות. That leaves רב פפא's view in place.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume every requirement for a גר also applies to a freed slave. Here the comparison is limited to טבילה only.

phrases.english: When that [phrase] was taught,
it was taught regarding immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא לְעִנְיַן טְבִילָה תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits which part of the ברייתא the phrase refers to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase means that a freed slave, like a גר, must accept the מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means only that both a גר and a freed slave need טבילה, so רב פפא's view holds.

steps.title: Dispute over what 'doing her nails' means
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about the יפת תואר shaving her head and 'doing' her nails. רבי אליעזר says she cuts them, and רבי עקיבא says she lets them grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And she shall shave her head and do her nails.' רבי אליעזר says: she cuts them. רבי עקיבא says: she lets them grow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the יפת תואר. Two תנאים argue about what the Torah means when it tells her to 'do' her nails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's word 'do' is unclear. It could mean trimming the nails or letting them grow long. רבי אליעזר says cutting, and רבי עקיבא says growing. The reasons come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish woman captured in war, whom a Jewish soldier may marry after a process the Torah sets out

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree she must shave her head. The argument is only about the nails.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And she shall shave her head
and do her nails."
Rabbi Eliezer says: she cuts them.
Rabbi Akiva says: she lets them grow.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְגִלְּחָה אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ וְעָשְׂתָה אֶת צִפׇּרְנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of קבלת מצוות for slaves and turns to the laws of the יפת תואר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: she cuts her nails. רבי עקיבא: she lets them grow.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reason: nails are like hair, so they are removed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר points out that the Torah uses 'doing' for both the head and the nails. Since the head is shaved, meaning the hair is removed, the nails are removed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: 'doing' is said about the head, and 'doing' is said about the nails. Just as there it means removing, so too here it means removing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר explains his view. He compares the nails to the head, which appear in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head's 'doing' is shaving, which removes the hair. רבי אליעזר says the shared feature is removal, so the nails must be cut. He reads the two parts of the פסוק as working the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as there... so too here': a comparison formula

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
'Doing' is stated about the head,
phrases.notes: The shaving of the head counts as a kind of 'doing' that the Torah asks of her.

phrases.english: and 'doing' is stated about the nails.
Just as there it means removal,
so too here it means removal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: נֶאֶמְרָה עֲשִׂיָּה בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבי אליעזר's view from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the nails must be cut
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison to the head in the same פסוק, where the hair is removed

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's reason: nails are like hair, so she is made unattractive
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא uses the same comparison but sees a different shared point. Shaving the head makes her unattractive, so the nails must also make her unattractive, meaning she lets them grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'doing' is said about the head, and 'doing' is said about the nails. Just as there it makes her unattractive, so too here it makes her unattractive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא explains his view. He uses the exact same comparison as רבי אליעזר but draws the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the head and nails are compared. They disagree about what the head's shaving is for. רבי אליעזר says the point is removal. רבי עקיבא says the point is making her unattractive, and long nails do that.

keyTerms.meaning: Making someone look unattractive or repulsive

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים use the same comparison. The argument is only about what the shaving of the head is meant to do.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'Doing' is stated about the head,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, so it reads just like רבי אליעזר's line.

phrases.english: and 'doing' is stated about the nails.
Just as there it makes her unattractive,
so too here it makes her unattractive.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: נֶאֶמְרָה עֲשִׂיָּה בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same comparison as step 14 but takes a different point from it.
steps.raayaObject: That she lets her nails grow
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison to the head, where shaving makes her unattractive

steps.title: Proof for רבי אליעזר from מפיבשת
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says מפיבשת did not 'do' his feet or his mustache. There, 'doing' clearly means trimming, which supports רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A proof for רבי אליעזר: 'And מפיבשת son of שאול came down to meet the king; he had not done his feet and had not done his mustache.' What does 'doing' mean there? Removal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from נביאים to support רבי אליעזר. It shows that 'doing' to nails and hair means trimming them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what 'doing' means. In the מפיבשת פסוק, not 'doing' his feet and mustache must mean he did not trim them. So 'doing' means removing, just as רבי אליעזר says.

keyTerms.meaning: מפיבשת, the son of יהונתן and grandson of שאול (the פסוק calls him 'son of שאול')

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah says the יפת תואר must 'do' her nails. רבי אליעזר says this means cutting, and רבי עקיבא says it means letting them grow. The פסוק about מפיבשת shows that 'doing' can mean trimming, which supports רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And a proof for the words of Rabbi Eliezer:
"And Mephibosheth, son of Saul,
came down to meet the king;
he had not done his feet
and had not done his mustache."
What is 'doing'? Removal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אליעזר's side of the dispute from steps 14-15.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that 'doing' nails means cutting them

steps.title: Opening a new ברייתא about her weeping for her parents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא on the פסוק 'and she shall weep for her father and her mother.' The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And she shall weep for her father and her mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא quotes the next part of the יפת תואר passage, and the ברייתא explains it on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the פסוק is quoted here. The ברייתא's explanation of what this weeping means continues past this line.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And she shall weep for her father and her mother."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וּבָכְתָה אֶת אָבִיהָ וְאֶת אִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next law in the יפת תואר passage after finishing the nails dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a ברייתא on the יפת תואר weeping for her parents; the ruling continues on the next amud.
